display.purpose: The page's single h1 only. Mixes upright and italic in one line.

title.purpose: Component-level headers (condition-card names, candidate-picker heading) — still serif.

body.purpose: Specs, captions, table cells, result text — set in mono, not sans.

label.purpose: Nav links, brand mark, buttons, chips, uppercase mono small-caps.

shadows.name: glass-float
shadows.purpose: Search-results dropdown and other floating panels, always paired with backdrop-filter blur.

shadows.name: tooltip-lift
shadows.purpose: Coverage-map hover tooltip — deeper than glass-float since it sits on inverted (dark) ground.

motion.name: ease-editorial
motion.purpose: The system's single easing curve — used for every transition and animation, first-load reveals and scroll-triggered reveals alike.

motion.name: lift-in
motion.purpose: First-load staged entrance for hero elements (headline, search, nav, scroll cue), each with its own delay.

motion.name: reveal-in
motion.purpose: Scroll-triggered entrance via IntersectionObserver for below-the-fold content; respects prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Quiver Chip
components.description: A ski committed to the quiver — solid ink fill, paper text, with an embedded length picker and remove button.
components.css: .ds-quiver-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.4rem; padding: 0.3rem 0.3rem 0.3rem 0.75rem; background: #101A22; color: #F4F7FA; border-radius: 100px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.6875rem; letter-spacing: 0.04em; list-style: none; } .ds-length-picker { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.625rem; color: #F4F7FA; background: rgba(244, 247, 250, 0.16); border: none; border-radius: 100px; padding: 0.15rem 0.35rem; } .ds-chip-remove { width: 21px; height: 21px; display: inline-grid; place-items: center; border: none; border-radius: 50%; cursor: pointer; background: rgba(244, 247, 250, 0.24); color: #F4F7FA; transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-chip-remove:hover { background: #F4F7FA; color: #101A22; }

components.name: Search Field
components.description: The hero's frosted-glass search input, sitting directly on the photograph.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.7rem; padding: 0 0.4rem 0 1rem; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.9); backdrop-filter: blur(10px) saturate(120%); border: 1px solid rgba(16, 26, 34, 0.16); border-radius: 100px; transition: border-color 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), box-shadow 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-field:focus-within { border-color: #101A22; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(16, 26, 34, 0.1); } .ds-field-icon { color: #5B7086; flex: none; } .ds-search-input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; border: none; background: none; outline: none; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; color: #101A22; caret-color: #C1372B; padding: 0.9rem 0.4rem 0.9rem 0; }

components.name: Toggle Button
components.description: Pill-shaped secondary action, e.g. 'View as table' — transparent at rest, ink border on hover.
components.css: .ds-toggle-btn { background: none; border: 1px solid rgba(16, 26, 34, 0.16); color: #2E4152; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.625rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 0.4rem 0.8rem; border-radius: 100px; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), color 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-toggle-btn:hover { border-color: #101A22; color: #101A22; }

components.name: Interest Chip
components.description: Single-select 'lean toward' bias chip — active state fills solid ink.
components.css: .ds-interest-chip { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.625rem; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #2E4152; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7); border: 1px solid rgba(16, 26, 34, 0.16); border-radius: 100px; padding: 0.35rem 0.75rem; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-interest-chip[aria-pressed='true'] { background: #101A22; border-color: #101A22; color: #F4F7FA; } .ds-interest-chip:hover { border-color: #2E4152; color: #101A22; }

narrative.overview: The full-bleed powder photograph isn't a hero image sitting on top of the page — it is the page ground. Charcoal serif type sits directly on the snow with no scrim, no gradient overlay, no darkening filter: the composition is chosen (crop, subject placement, copy column position) so the photo's own contrast carries the text, measured against the actual pixels rather than assumed. That single technical move — treating the photograph as substrate rather than decoration — is what separates this from a conventional hero-image-plus-headline web pattern and gives the whole system its editorial, print-magazine register rather than a software-product one. Everything below the fold continues that voice: slender serif display type (Cormorant Garamond) that mixes upright and italic within a single line for emphasis, paired with a small, restrained monospace (IBM Plex Mono) for every functional and labeling role. This is explicitly a photo-led, editorial-first system, built as a deliberate alternative to root's data-dense Instrument Panel world, wrapped in a voice built for a wider public audience.
keyCharacteristics: The photograph is page ground, not hero decoration — text sits directly on it with no scrim, contrast-checked against real pixels
Two-typeface system with a strict division of labor: serif for reading, mono for scanning/acting
Near-flat elevation — depth comes from ink/paper contrast and hairline borders, not shadows; the exception is a small set of floating elements that use frosted glass plus a soft shadow
One accent color (Jacket Red, drawn from the photograph itself) used sparingly for the single most important word or number on a given screen
The same reserved status vocabulary (good/warning/critical) as the incumbent system, re-expressed in this palette rather than reinvented
Pill shapes everywhere something is actionable or a chip; small, sharp corners (4px) everywhere something is a static card

rules.name: The Photograph-as-Ground Rule
rules.body: The hero photograph is never darkened, scrimmed, or gradient-overlaid to force contrast — text placement and color are chosen so the photo's own pixels already carry the required contrast, verified per-composition. A new hero image or crop is evaluated the same way, not patched with an overlay.

rules.name: The Reference Palette Rule
rules.body: Status colors trace to a fixed external dataviz reference palette, not to this system's own ink/paper scale. Don't re-harmonize them to match; changing them means redoing the dataviz methodology, not a color-matching pass.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Serif reads; mono scans and acts. A new component's copy defaults to mono unless it is genuinely prose meant to be read start-to-finish, in which case it's serif — never a third typeface, never sans-serif.

rules.name: The No-Bare-Number Rule
rules.body: The derived temperament score is never shown as a bare figure — always a short phrase plus a position-on-spectrum gauge, with the raw number kept as small secondary detail.

rules.name: The Flat-With-Glass Rule
rules.body: Nothing that sits in the normal page flow gets a shadow — depth there comes from ink/paper contrast alone. Shadow is reserved for elements that float over content (dropdowns, tooltips) and is always paired with backdrop blur on those, never used alone.

dos: Do verify a hero photograph's contrast against its actual pixels before committing a text color — no scrim or overlay is a fallback for a composition that doesn't hold contrast on its own
Do keep serif for reading and mono for scanning/acting — never blend the two roles on the same element
Do reserve shadow for elements that float over content, always paired with backdrop blur
Do design the mobile hero as its own independently-composed crop, not a scaled-down version of the desktop composition
Do carry over every accessibility and coverage-model invariant from root's system unchanged — this is a re-skin of the product, not a re-design of it
donts: Don't add a scrim, gradient overlay, or darkening filter to the hero photograph to force text contrast — recompose or recrop instead
Don't use a third typeface, or use the serif for functional/label text or the mono for reading-prose text
Don't apply a shadow to a component that sits flat in the page flow (condition cards, chips, section panels) — only floating-over-content elements get one
Don't re-harmonize the status colors to this system's ink/paper palette — they're pinned to the external dataviz reference
Don't widen the corner-radius scale beyond pill/4px/10-14px without a real new use case — the binary is deliberate
